headline: Hydrogen is the simplest and most abundant element in the universe—the stuff stars are made of
universal_truth: Simple building blocks can create infinite complexity
fun_facts: Hydrogen makes up 75% of all matter in the universe—stars are mostly burning hydrogen
Two hydrogen atoms plus one oxygen atom equals water—the molecule that makes life possible
The Sun converts 600 million tons of hydrogen into helium every second
discussion_questions: How can the simplest thing be the foundation of everything complex?
What simple elements in your life combine to create something essential?
Why do you think the universe started with the simplest element?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: One proton. One electron. That's it—the simplest atom possible. Yet hydrogen is the most abundant element in the universe, the fuel of stars, and half the recipe for water. From ultimate simplicity comes the foundation of everything.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: The universe is 75% hydrogen—but Earth has relatively little free hydrogen. Where did our hydrogen go? And why is this simplest element so fundamental to life?
cliff.prompt: Why is hydrogen essential to life on Earth?

options.text: Hydrogen combines with oxygen to form water—without it, no liquid water, no life
options.response: Yes. Two hydrogen atoms bonded to oxygen create water—the medium of life.

options.text: Hydrogen provides the energy that powers all cellular processes
options.response: Hydrogen is involved in energy processes, but its most essential role is in water...

q1.title: Cosmic Abundance
q1.script: After the Big Bang, the universe was almost entirely hydrogen. Over 13.8 billion years, stars fused hydrogen into heavier elements. But hydrogen remains dominant—75% of all matter. Everything started simple.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Cosmic Abundance"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Star Fuel
q2.script: The Sun converts 600 million tons of hydrogen into helium every second through nuclear fusion. This process releases the energy that warms Earth and powers photosynthesis. The light reaching your eyes right now began as hydrogen.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Water's Recipe
q3.script: Take two hydrogen atoms. Add one oxygen atom. You get water—the molecule that fills oceans, flows through your body, and makes life possible. The simplest element combines to create the most essential compound.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Simplicity is not weakness. Hydrogen teaches that the most fundamental building blocks—simple, humble, overlooked—can combine to create stars, oceans, and life itself. Never underestimate simple foundations.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 75. Tomorrow, we'll explore the building blocks of everything—atoms and molecules. Until then, drink some water—and taste hydrogen's contribution.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Simple Foundations - Identify Your Building Blocks
growTrack.learning_objective: Recognize the simple elements that create complex results
growTrack.activity: What are the simplest 'elements' of your good days—sleep, movement, connection, purpose? Like hydrogen combining to form water, what simple habits combine to create your wellbeing? Identify your essential two or three.
